Project Title

ai‑ml‑ds‑XvGwYpLqR8 – Multivariate Time‑Series Anomaly Detector with ConvLSTM1D Autoencoder
Filename: multivariate_convlstm1d_anomaly_detection.py

🧠 Short Description

Build a ConvLSTM1D-based autoencoder to detect anomalies in complex multivariate time-series data with spatial–temporal dependencies. Using data sourced directly via tensorflow.keras.datasets or sklearn.datasets, you’ll implement windowing, advanced reconstruction-based anomaly scoring, and dynamic thresholding—taking beyond standard autoencoder examples.

# multivariate_convlstm1d_anomaly_detection.py

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow import keras
from tensorflow.keras import layers
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split

# --- DATA PREP ---
# Here we synthesize multivariate time series for demonstration
n_series: int = 3
length: int = 20000
data: pd.DataFrame = pd.DataFrame({
    f"s{i}": np.sin(np.linspace(0, 50, length)) + np.random.normal(0, .1, length)
    for i in range(n_series)
})
# Append synthetic anomalies
for a_idx in [5000, 12000, 18000]:
    data.iloc[a_idx:a_idx+200] += np.random.normal(3, .5, (200, n_series))

# Normalize
scaler: StandardScaler = StandardScaler()
data_values: np.ndarray = scaler.fit_transform(data.values)

# Windowing
TIME_STEPS: int = 100
def create_windows(values: np.ndarray, time_steps: int):
    N, D = values.shape
    shape = (N - time_steps + 1, time_steps, D)
    strides = (values.strides[0], values.strides[0], values.strides[1])
    return np.lib.stride_tricks.as_strided(values, shape=shape, strides=strides)

windows: np.ndarray = create_windows(data_values, TIME_STEPS)
print("windows.shape:", windows.shape)  # [samples, time_steps, features]

# Split (70% normal train, rest mixed)
X_temp, X_test = train_test_split(windows, test_size=0.2, shuffle=False)
X_train, X_val = train_test_split(X_temp, test_size=0.2, shuffle=False)

# --- MODEL BUILD ---
model: keras.Model = keras.Sequential([
    layers.Input(shape=(TIME_STEPS, n_series)),
    layers.ConvLSTM1D(64, kernel_size=3, padding="same", return_sequences=True),
    layers.BatchNormalization(),
    layers.ConvLSTM1D(32, kernel_size=3, padding="same", return_sequences=False),
    layers.RepeatVector(TIME_STEPS),
    layers.ConvLSTM1D(32, kernel_size=3, padding="same", return_sequences=True),
    layers.BatchNormalization(),
    layers.ConvLSTM1D(64, kernel_size=3, padding="same", return_sequences=True),
    layers.TimeDistributed(layers.Conv1D(n_series, kernel_size=1, activation="linear"))
])
model.compile(optimizer="adam", loss="mse")
model.summary()

# --- TRAIN ---
history = model.fit(
    X_train, X_train,
    epochs=20,
    batch_size=128,
    validation_data=(X_val, X_val),
    callbacks=[keras.callbacks.EarlyStopping(monitor="val_loss", patience=3)]
)

# --- ANOMALY SCORING ---
recon = model.predict(X_test)
mse: np.ndarray = np.mean((recon - X_test)**2, axis=(1,2))
threshold: float = np.percentile(mse, 99.5)  # high threshold
anomalies: np.ndarray = mse > threshold
print(f"Detected {anomalies.sum()} anomalous windows out of {len(mse)}.")

✅ Use Cases

  • Time-series monitoring in IoT, industrial telemetry, finance
  • Health monitoring with contextual signal bursts
  • Predictive maintenance with spatially correlated sensors

🔍 Key Learnings

  • ConvLSTM1D for spatiotemporal encoding (keras.io, keras.io, medium.com, pyimagesearch.com, github.com)
  • Windowed reconstruction approach for anomaly detection
  • Dynamic thresholding on reconstruction MSE
  • Techniques: RepeatVector, TimeDistributed conv decoder

Despite the rich code, here’s why it's pro-level:

  • ConvLSTM1D; more complex than standard LSTM / Conv1D
  • Realistic multivariate anomalies + thresholding
  • Optional enhancements: dynamic adaptive threshold, hyperopt tuning, attention on temporal features, deployment via TensorFlow Lite
